report_title: Brand architecture: Example Booking and its four products

windows.dataforseo: average monthly US searches, location_code 2840, language_code en

header.sources: Pasted portfolio, customer mix, prices and risk answers; Search Console (2 properties); DataForSEO (1 call); GA4 (2 calls); Google Ads (1 call). Meta Ads not connected.

thresholds.equity_none: R < 0.05 or under 50 searches a month, or planned
thresholds.audience: same >= 0.6, partial 0.3 to 0.6, different < 0.3 (segments with 10%+ of parent customers)
thresholds.price: same band 0.5 to 2, different above 3 or below 1/3
thresholds.collision: 500+ US searches a month and under 10% click share
thresholds.ads_own_brand_campaign: 30+ clicks on the name's searches in the window

header.parent_spend_basis: plan mix Starter 40%, Growth 45%, Business 15% at $19, $49, $99

headline: Keep Example Booking as the master brand and make five naming changes: fold TapDeposit into it as Example Booking Payments, turn Shiftnest from a separate brand into an endorsed one ("Shiftnest by Example Booking"), launch Clinic Suite as Example Booking Clinic Suite, rename the Refill feature to Waitlist auto-fill, and rename Shiftnest's Team plan to Plus. Only Glowfinder earns a separate brand, because its buyers are consumers and it rates your own customers.

portfolio.current: its own coined name, sold inside the Example Booking site and app
run as a separate brand; its site and app do not mention Example Booking

evidence: Name demand: 30 US searches a month for the name alone against 3,070 for Example Booking, so R is 0.01: equity none.
Co-search: 84% of Search Console impressions for its name also contain Example Booking.
Audience: 94% of its buyers are in segments that hold at least 10% of Example Booking customers (clinics, fitness studios and trainers, salons), so A is 0.94: same.
Price: $65.00 a month per customer against $44.50 for Example Booking, so Q is 1.46: same band.
Risk: no on all three questions.
per_product.what_changes_now: Retire the TapDeposit name and call it Example Booking Payments. Only 30 people a month search the name, and 84% of the searches that do include it already say Example Booking. Its pages drew 3,079 sessions and 36 key events in 90 days (1.17% against 2.52% on the rest of example.com).

per_product.recommendation: endorsed brand: Shiftnest by Example Booking
evidence: Name demand: 1,370 US searches a month for the name alone against 3,070 for Example Booking, so R is 0.446: equity strong.
Co-search: 3% of Search Console impressions for its name also contain Example Booking.
Audience: 37% of its buyers are in segments that hold at least 10% of Example Booking customers (clinics, fitness studios and trainers, salons), so A is 0.37: partial.
Price: $44.00 a month per customer against $44.50 for Example Booking, so Q is 0.99: same band.
Risk: no on all three questions.
per_product.what_changes_now: Keep the Shiftnest name and add "by Example Booking" to the logo lockup, site header, app store listing and ads. Its name is searched 1,370 times a month (R 0.446), and its own name searches convert at 17.1% in Google Ads, 4.3 times the non-brand rate. Merging it into Example Booking would throw that away. A separate brand isn't justified either: A is 0.37, partial rather than different, and only 4.8% of its sessions come from example.com today, so the parent's backing is unused.

evidence: Planned, so equity is none; the name alone has 210 US searches a month today.
Audience: 100% of its buyers are in segments that hold at least 10% of Example Booking customers (clinics, fitness studios and trainers, salons), so A is 1.0: same.
Price: $1,047.00 a month per customer against $44.50 for Example Booking, so Q is 23.53: different, price up.
Risk: no on all three questions.
per_product.what_changes_now: Launch it as Example Booking Clinic Suite. Its price is 23.53 times the parent's, which makes it eligible for a separate brand on price alone, but the price is going up and the buyers are clinics who already know the parent (Search Console shows 2,200 impressions in 90 days for Example Booking searches that mention clinics).

evidence: Planned, so equity is none; the name alone has 10 US searches a month today.
Audience: 0% of its buyers are in segments that hold at least 10% of Example Booking customers (clinics, fitness studios and trainers, salons), so A is 0.0: different.
Price: $0.00 a month per customer against $44.50 for Example Booking, so Q is 0.0: different, price down.
Risk: yes, it rates salons and lists rival salons next to the parent's own salon customers.
per_product.what_changes_now: Build Glowfinder as a separate brand with its own site, app listing, ad campaigns and social accounts. Its buyers are consumers (A 0.0), and it rates the salons that pay Example Booking. Example Booking appears only in its legal and about pages. You confirmed the funding for a second brand.

products.master_brand: Example Booking + a plain descriptor (Payments, Reminders)
products.sub_brand: Example Booking + a line name, for a line priced well above the core plans (Clinic Suite)
products.separate: own name, no parent mention outside legal and about pages (Glowfinder)

tiers.action: keep; Example Booking Payments and Example Booking Clinic Suite use no separate tier names
rename Team to Plus so the set reads Basic, Plus, Pro on one axis (endorsed brands keep their own tier names)

features.why: not sold on its own, so it gets a descriptive name; the coined name also collides (see collisions)
already descriptive; sits under Payments after the rename

naming_system.new_product_rule: A new product carries the Example Booking name unless its buyers are a different audience (A under 0.3), its price is above 3 times or below a third of $44.50 a month, or a risk answer is yes. Clinic Suite and Glowfinder were run through it here.
naming_system.trademark: Clearing Glowfinder, Clinic Suite and the Shiftnest endorsement is your step (USPTO search); this report does not clear any name.

channel_plan.website: pages move into the main navigation under Features; the URL change goes to SEO (hand-off 1)
channel_plan.ads: TapDeposit searches drew 6 clicks in 90 days (under 30), so they stay in the Example Booking brand campaign; ads say Example Booking Payments

channel_plan.website: stays on shiftnest.example with "by Example Booking" in the header and footer and a link to example.com; no domain move implied
channel_plan.ads: Shiftnest searches drew 416 clicks in 90 days, so it keeps its own brand campaign; add "by Example Booking" to ad text and sitelinks
channel_plan.social: keeps its own accounts (cafes and retail are not Example Booking's audience); bios name Example Booking

channel_plan.website: its own section and nav item on example.com
channel_plan.ads: Clinic Suite searches drew 0 clicks in 90 days (planned, under 30), so its terms start in the Example Booking brand campaign; give it its own ad group there once "example booking clinic suite" searches pass 30 clicks in a 90-day window. Generic clinic terms stay in the clinic campaign
channel_plan.social: Example Booking accounts, with a clinic content series

channel_plan.website: its own site and app listings (the domain choice is yours and SEO's)
channel_plan.ads: its own campaigns in a separate ad account (consumer audience, different billing)
channel_plan.social: its own accounts, never cross-posted from Example Booking

seo_handoffs.move: rename TapDeposit to Example Booking Payments: the /tapdeposit/ section moves to a payments URL
seo_handoffs.go_to: site-migration-monitor and internal-linking-planner if installed, or your SEO lead

shiftnest.example.note: endorsed brands can stay on their own domain, so no move is recommended. If you ever consider folding it into the main site, start from these numbers with SEO.

unknowns: Meta Ads is not connected, so the audience overlap was not cross-checked against ad results by age and gender; A comes from the pasted customer mix.

Search Console hides rare queries, so its click and impression counts are floors. The co-search shares (C) are built from those counts and can sit above or below the true share, because hidden rows fall on both sides of each share.
